verses.1: He ruled for forty years. He also ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. But he did not do what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, just like his father David did.
verses.2: And he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and also made vessels for wives.
verses.3: And he set fire to the valley of Ben-Hinnom, and he burned his children in the fire, just as the nations were destroyed by God from before the children of Israel.
verses.4: And he burned and destroyed them in the flames, on the hillsides, and under every tree.
verses.5: And Jehovah, his God, gave it into the hands of the king of Aram. They used it to fight against them. Then they were defeated by great destruction. And also, in the hands of the king of Israel, it was used to wage a great war.
verses.6: And Pekah son of Remaliah killed one hundred and ten thousand people in Judah in one day. All these people were soldiers who abandoned Jehovah, the God of their ancestors.
verses.7: And Zichri, the king of Ephraim, killed his son, as well as Azrikam, the chief priest, and Elnana, one of the kings’ sons.
verses.8: And the children of Israel gathered together from their homes. There were thousands of women, both daughters and sons. They also brought along a large amount of livestock with them. They brought this livestock to Shechem for protection.
verses.9: And there was a prophet of Jehovah who went before the people who came to Jerusalem. He said to them, “In the heat of Jehovah, God of your ancestors, over Judah, they were handed over into your hands. And they were killed by you in anger, up to the heavens.”
verses.10: And now, sons of Judah and Jerusalem, you say that you want to serve your slaves and wives. But not only you, but also those who are with you are responsible for obeying the LORD your God.
verses.11: And now, listen to me. Restore those who have been taken away from your brothers. For Jehovah has punished you for this.
verses.12: And the men from the heads of the sons of Ephraim were: Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshullam, and Jechizkiah son of Shallum. They stood against those who came from the city.
verses.13: And they said to them, “Do not bring those sacrifices here now. For it is the judgment of Jehovah upon us. You are saying that we should be punished for our sins and for our wrongdoing. Our sins are too great, and there is also punishment for Israel.”
verses.14: And He left the sacrifices and the offerings in front of the priests and all the people.
verses.15: And those men who were called by his name stood up. They held their swords and all their weapons. They decorated them with decorations of gold. They wore them on their bodies. They ate and drank from them. They used them for various purposes. They also brought them to the city of Temarim, along with their ancestors. Then they returned to Shomron.
verses.16: On that day, the king sent Ahaz to help him with the kings of Assyria.
verses.17: And still, they came and attacked Judah. They settled there and became its inhabitants.
verses.18: And the Philistines captured the cities of Samaria and Judea. They took captive the Temple of Shemesh, Airolon, Gederot, Shokho, and their daughters. They also took Timna and her daughters, Gemzo, and their daughters. They settled there.
verses.19: For Jehovah has defeated Judah through the king of Israel. He has caused harm to Judah, and he is now above them all.
verses.20: And the king of Assyria, Sennacherib, came against him. He tried to defeat him, but he couldn’t do so.
verses.21: For he took possession of the House of God and the palace of the king and the officials. He gave it to the king of Assyria, but not to Ezer.
verses.22: And in those times of difficulty, when he was in need, it became his duty to serve God. He was the king Ahaz.
verses.23: And he worshiped the gods of Damscak, who were those who caused people to suffer. He said, “These are the gods of the kings of Aram. They will help them in their suffering. They will also help me. They were meant to be their rulers and to rule over all Israel.”
verses.24: And he gathered all the utensils of the Temple together. He sealed up all the doors of the Temple. Then he made altars in every corner of Jerusalem.
verses.25: And in every city and town of Judah, he caused others to be killed as sacrifices to other gods. He angered the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
verses.26: And all his other words and all his former and later ways are recorded in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
verses.27: And Ahaz lay down with his fathers. He was buried in the city of Jerusalem, because he did not bring him to the tombs of the kings of Israel. Jehoshaphat, his son, became king after him.
